chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The woman giving disavowment (mubarat) says to her husband: 'For you is what is upon you, and disavow me,' and he leaves her.
I said: 'So he says to her: 'If you retract regarding something, then I am in control of your body (for intimacy).'

key_terms.الْمُبَارِئَةُ: The woman initiating the disavowment divorce
key_terms.لَكَ مَا عَلَيْكَ: For you is what is upon you (referring to the dowry/debt)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific verbal formulas and legal consequences of Al-Mubarat divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanics of Al-Mubarat, a mutual divorce where the wife initiates release by offering to forfeit her dowry (Mubarat) to the husband. The dialogue highlights the husband's acceptance and his retained right to intimate relations (Imlak al-Bu'd) if she retracts the divorce before the Iddah expires, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the irrevocability and conditions of this specific divorce type. It underscores the consensual yet financially weighted nature of dissolving the marriage bond in early Shia legal tradition.
